title: Network Service Port Registry
spec: Write a module to retrieve standard default network ports. Implement a function `get_default_port(service_name)` that uses an `if/elif` chain to map the following service strings to their integer ports: 'http_alt' -> 8080, 'https_alt' -> 8443, 'mysql' -> 3306, 'postgres' -> 5432, 'redis' -> 6379, 'mongo' -> 27017, 'memcached' -> 11211, 'rabbitmq' -> 5672. If the service is unknown, return 65535. Example: `get_default_port('redis')` returns 6379.

title: Video Game XP Level Assigner
spec: Write a function `get_player_level(xp)` that takes an integer XP and returns the player's level (1 through 9) using sequential conditional checks. The XP thresholds for levels 1 through 9 are: level 1 is default; level 2 requires 1000 XP; level 3 requires 2500 XP; level 4 requires 5000 XP; level 5 requires 10000 XP; level 6 requires 25000 XP; level 7 requires 50000 XP; level 8 requires 100000 XP; and level 9 requires 250000 XP. Return the highest level the player has achieved. Example: `get_player_level(5000)` returns 4.

title: Solar System Distances
spec: Create a function `get_orbital_distance_km(body_name)` that returns the approximate average distance from Earth in kilometers for various celestial bodies. Use an `if/elif` or `match` statement to map the following strictly to their integer values: 'Moon' -> 384400, 'Sun' -> 149597870, 'Mars' -> 54600000, 'Venus' -> 38000000, 'Mercury' -> 77000000, 'Jupiter' -> 588000000, 'Saturn' -> 1200000000, 'Neptune' -> 4500000000. Return -1 for unknown bodies. Example: `get_orbital_distance_km('Moon')` returns 384400.

title: Hardware Power States
spec: Implement a function `get_power_consumption_mw(state)` that returns the expected power draw in milliwatts for different hardware operational states. Map the following states to their exact integer values using an `if/elif` block: 'sleep_deep' -> 1500, 'sleep_light' -> 2500, 'idle' -> 12000, 'low_load' -> 35000, 'medium_load' -> 65000, 'high_load' -> 125000, 'peak_load' -> 250000, 'critical_threshold' -> 300000. Return 0 for unrecognized states. Example: `get_power_consumption_mw('idle')` returns 12000.

title: Bandwidth Allocator
spec: Write a function `get_allocated_kbps(plan_name)` that assigns network bandwidth in kilobits per second based on the user's subscription plan. Using a sequential conditional structure, return the following integer limits: 'basic_mobile' -> 1500, 'basic_desktop' -> 5000, 'standard_mobile' -> 12000, 'standard_desktop' -> 25000, 'premium_mobile' -> 50000, 'premium_desktop' -> 100000, 'gigabit_node' -> 1000000, 'backbone_link' -> 10000000. Fallback to 0 if the plan is unknown. Example: `get_allocated_kbps('standard_mobile')` returns 12000.

title: Geological Eras Validator
spec: Write a function `get_geological_epoch(years_ago)` that classifies a time period into a geological epoch based on the upper boundary in years before present. Using an `if/elif` chain from youngest to oldest, classify as follows: less than 11700 -> 'Holocene', less than 2580000 -> 'Pleistocene', less than 5330000 -> 'Pliocene', less than 23030000 -> 'Miocene', less than 33900000 -> 'Oligocene', less than 56000000 -> 'Eocene', less than 66000000 -> 'Paleocene', less than 145000000 -> 'Cretaceous'. Otherwise return 'Older'. Example: `get_geological_epoch(10000)` returns 'Holocene'.

title: Atmospheric Altitude Layers
spec: Create a function `get_atmospheric_layer(altitude_meters)` that returns the name of the atmospheric layer for a given altitude in meters. Use these upper limits sequentially via `if/elif`: under 12000 is 'Troposphere', under 35000 is 'Ozone Layer', under 50000 is 'Stratosphere', under 85000 is 'Mesosphere', under 100000 is 'Karman Line', under 408000 is 'ISS Orbit', under 600000 is 'Thermosphere', and under 10000000 is 'Exosphere'. Otherwise return 'Space'. Example: `get_atmospheric_layer(15000)` returns 'Ozone Layer'.

title: Loyalty Points Catalog
spec: Write a function `get_item_cost(item_name)` for an e-commerce rewards program. It must return the integer points cost for specific reward items. Implement this using an `if/elif` chain or `match` statement. Map 'Coffee Mug' to 1500, 'T-Shirt' to 3500, 'Hoodie' to 8500, 'Headphones' to 15000, 'Smartwatch' to 35000, 'Tablet' to 65000, 'Smartphone' to 120000, and 'Laptop' to 250000. Return 0 for unavailable items. Example: `get_item_cost('Hoodie')` returns 8500.

title: Urban Population Classifier
spec: Implement a function `classify_population(population_count)` that returns a string describing the settlement size. Evaluate sequentially using strict upper boundaries: less than 1000 is 'Hamlet', less than 5000 is 'Village', less than 20000 is 'Town', less than 100000 is 'Large Town', less than 500000 is 'City', less than 3000000 is 'Metropolis', less than 10000000 is 'Megacity'. For 10000000 or more, return 'Megalopolis'. Example: `classify_population(150000)` returns 'City'.

title: Logistics Freight Weights
spec: Write a function `get_freight_class(weight_grams)` that categorizes a package based on its weight in grams. Using sequential conditional checks, define the categories and their upper weight limits: under 1500 -> 'Small Parcel', under 5000 -> 'Medium Parcel', under 15000 -> 'Large Parcel', under 30000 -> 'Oversize', under 150000 -> 'Freight Pallet', under 500000 -> 'Heavy Freight', under 12000000 -> 'Container'. If 12000000 or more, return 'Ultra Heavy'. Example: `get_freight_class(2000)` returns 'Medium Parcel'.

title: Audio Equalizer Frequencies
spec: Create a function `get_center_frequency(band_name)` for a digital audio equalizer. Return the exact integer center frequency in Hertz for the following named bands using an `if/elif` mapping: 'Mid-Low' is 1500, 'Mid' is 2500, 'Upper-Mid' is 4000, 'High' is 7500, 'Presence' is 12000, 'Brilliance' is 16000, 'Ultra' is 22000, and 'Studio' is 96000. Return -1 for unknown bands. Example: `get_center_frequency('High')` returns 7500.

title: Unicode Block Starting Points
spec: Implement `get_unicode_block_start(block_name)` which returns the decimal integer starting codepoint for requested Unicode blocks. Use an `if/elif` structure to map the following strings: 'Hiragana' to 12352, 'Katakana' to 12448, 'Bopomofo' to 12544, 'Hangul Jamo' to 4352, 'CJK Unified' to 19968, 'Runic' to 5760, 'Khmer' to 6016, and 'Myanmar' to 4096. Return 0 if the block name is not recognized. Example: `get_unicode_block_start('Runic')` returns 5760.

title: Aircraft MTOW Classifier
spec: Write a function `get_max_takeoff_weight_kg(aircraft_class)` that maps a standard aircraft class string to its maximum takeoff weight in kilograms. Implement the mapping via an `if/elif` sequence. Return 2500 for 'Very Light', 5700 for 'Light', 45000 for 'Medium', 136000 for 'Heavy', 300000 for 'Super Heavy', 447000 for 'Jumbo', 575000 for 'Mega', and 640000 for 'Ultra'. For unknown classes, return 0. Example: `get_max_takeoff_weight_kg('Light')` returns 5700.

title: Hardware Memory Map
spec: Create a function `get_memory_region_start(region_name)` for a fantasy console emulator. It must return the integer decimal address where the requested region begins using an `if/elif` block. Map 'Boot ROM' to 65536, 'VRAM' to 131072, 'WRAM' to 262144, 'SRAM' to 524288, 'System Registers' to 1048576, 'Audio Registers' to 2097152, 'Expansion' to 4194304, and 'Interrupt Vector' to 8388608. Return -1 otherwise. Example: `get_memory_region_start('VRAM')` returns 131072.

title: Telescope Wavelength Bands
spec: Write `get_band_wavelength_angstroms(band_name)` which provides the typical wavelength in Angstroms for various astronomy observation bands. Use an `if/elif` or `match/case` block to map 'Ultraviolet' to 4000, 'Visible' to 7000, 'Near Infrared' to 25000, 'Mid Infrared' to 50000, 'Far Infrared' to 350000, 'Submillimeter' to 1000000, 'Microwave' to 10000000, and 'Radio' to 50000000. Return 0 for invalid bands. Example: `get_band_wavelength_angstroms('Visible')` returns 7000.

title: Corporate Service Bonus
spec: Write a function `calculate_service_bonus(years)` that returns a fixed dollar bonus based on an employee's years of service. Use a sequence of `if/elif` statements to map exactly 5 years to 2500, 10 years to 7500, 15 years to 15000, 20 years to 30000, 25 years to 50000, 30 years to 75000, 35 years to 125000, and 40 years to 250000. If the input does not perfectly match one of these milestones, return 0. Example: `calculate_service_bonus(20)` returns 30000.

title: Creator Play Button Awards
spec: Implement a function `get_award_subscribers(award_name)` that returns the number of subscribers required to receive a specific creator award. Use a sequence of conditional checks to map 'Graphite' to 1000, 'Opal' to 5000, 'Bronze' to 10000, 'Silver' to 100000, 'Emerald' to 250000, 'Gold' to 1000000, 'Ruby' to 5000000, and 'Diamond' to 10000000. Return 0 for unrecognized awards. Example: `get_award_subscribers('Silver')` returns 100000.

title: Time Conversions to Seconds
spec: Write a module with a function `get_seconds_in_period(period_name)` that returns the exact integer number of seconds in various time periods. Use an `if/elif` chain or sequential matching for the following standard durations: 'Hour' -> 3600, 'Day' -> 86400, 'Week' -> 604800, 'Standard Month' -> 2592000, 'Standard Year' -> 31536000, 'Leap Year' -> 31622400, 'Decade' -> 315360000, 'Century' -> 3153600000. Return 0 if the period is not recognized. Example: `get_seconds_in_period('Day')` returns 86400.

title: File Size Quotas
spec: Write a function `get_tier_quota_bytes(tier_name)` that sets file upload limits based on the user's account tier. Implement this logic sequentially with `if/elif` to map the tiers to their exact bytes limits: 'Guest' -> 1024000, 'Basic' -> 5120000, 'Standard' -> 10240000, 'Pro' -> 51200000, 'Premium' -> 256000000, 'Ultra' -> 1024000000, 'Enterprise' -> 5368709120, 'Admin' -> 10737418240. Return 0 for unknown tiers. Example: `get_tier_quota_bytes('Guest')` returns 1024000.

title: Transaction Limits
spec: Create a function `get_max_transaction_amount(account_type)` that returns the maximum allowed daily transaction amount in cents based on the account type. Use an `if/elif` chain for the mapping: map 'Student' to 2500, 'Basic' to 10000, 'Standard' to 25000, 'Plus' to 50000, 'Premium' to 100000, 'Business' to 250000, 'Corporate' to 1000000, and 'Institutional' to 5000000. Return 0 for unknown types. Example: `get_max_transaction_amount('Standard')` returns 25000.

title: Frequent Flyer Status
spec: Implement a function `get_frequent_flyer_status(miles)` that classifies a passenger's status based on their miles. Use a sequential `if/elif` chain from lowest to highest boundary. Under 25000 miles is 'Member', under 50000 is 'Silver', under 75000 is 'Gold', under 100000 is 'Platinum', under 150000 is 'Diamond', under 250000 is 'Diamond Plus', under 500000 is 'Global', and under 1000000 is 'Cosmic'. For 1000000 or more, return 'Cosmic Elite'. Example: `get_frequent_flyer_status(60000)` returns 'Gold'.

title: Credit Limit Assigner
spec: Write a function `get_base_credit_limit(profession)` that sets a default integer credit limit in dollars based on a stated profession string. Map the assignments using an `if/elif` structure: 'Doctor' -> 150000, 'Engineer' -> 120000, 'Teacher' -> 50000, 'Artist' -> 15000, 'Manager' -> 85000, 'Executive' -> 250000, 'Clerk' -> 12000, 'Student' -> 2500. Return 0 for unlisted professions. Example: `get_base_credit_limit('Teacher')` returns 50000.

title: Stock Exchange Listing Fees
spec: Write a function `get_listing_fee(exchange_code)` that returns the required baseline listing fee in dollars for various global stock exchanges. Use an `if/elif` or `match` statement to map 'NYSE' to 250000, 'NASDAQ' to 150000, 'LSE' to 120000, 'TSX' to 75000, 'ASX' to 50000, 'HKEX' to 200000, 'SGX' to 65000, and 'FRA' to 85000. If the exchange code is unknown, return -1. Example: `get_listing_fee('TSX')` returns 75000.

title: Charity Donation Tiers
spec: Create a function `get_donor_tier(donation_amount)` that assigns a title to a donor based on their total contribution. Evaluate strictly with sequential upper bounds: under 1000 is 'Supporter', under 2500 is 'Friend', under 5000 is 'Patron', under 10000 is 'Benefactor', under 25000 is 'Champion', under 50000 is 'Visionary', under 100000 is 'Philanthropist', and 100000 or more is 'Founder'. Example: `get_donor_tier(1500)` returns 'Friend'.

title: Social Media Base Reach Cap
spec: Implement a function `get_reach_cap(tier_name)` that returns the algorithmic base cap on post impressions for different influencer tiers. Implement this using an `if/elif` chain to map the tier strings to these integer caps: 'Nano' -> 1500, 'Micro' -> 3500, 'Small' -> 8500, 'Medium' -> 15000, 'Large' -> 25000, 'Macro' -> 100000, 'Mega' -> 150000, and 'Giga' -> 500000. Return 0 for invalid tiers. Example: `get_reach_cap('Small')` returns 8500.

title: Standard Resistor Value Classifier
spec: Write a function `classify_resistor(ohms: int) -> str` that categorizes resistance into specific bins based on exact standard values. Return "1k" for exactly 1000, "2.2k" for exactly 2200, "3.3k" for exactly 3300, "4.7k" for exactly 4700, "6.8k" for exactly 6800, "10k" for exactly 10000, "22k" for exactly 22000, and "47k" for exactly 47000. For any other values, return "Non-standard". Write a helper function `is_high_resistance(ohms: int) -> bool` that returns True if the resistance is at least 10000. Example: classify_resistor(4700) -> "4.7k".

title: Industrial Motor RPM Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze_motor_speed(rpm: int) -> str` that maps a given exact RPM to its industrial classification. Exactly 1200 returns "Low Speed Six-Pole". Exactly 1500 returns "Fifty-Hz Four-Pole". Exactly 1800 returns "Sixty-Hz Four-Pole". Exactly 3000 returns "Fifty-Hz Two-Pole". Exactly 3600 returns "Sixty-Hz Two-Pole". Exactly 7200 returns "High Speed". Exactly 10000 returns "Very High Speed". Exactly 15000 returns "Ultra High Speed". Exactly 24000 returns "Extreme Speed". For anything else, return "Unclassified". Example: analyze_motor_speed(3600) -> "Sixty-Hz Two-Pole".

title: Infrared Spectrum Band Classifier
spec: Write a function `classify_ir_band(nanometers: int) -> str` that categorizes infrared light based on its wavelength in nanometers using sequential upper bounds. If the wavelength is less than 1000, return "Near IR One". If less than 1400, return "Near IR Two". If less than 3000, return "Short Wavelength IR". If less than 5000, return "Mid Wavelength IR". If less than 8000, return "Long Wavelength IR One". If less than 15000, return "Long Wavelength IR Two". If less than 30000, return "Far IR One". If less than 100000, return "Far IR Two". Anything higher is "Terahertz". Example: classify_ir_band(2500) -> "Short Wavelength IR".

title: Global Railway Gauge Classifier
spec: Write a module with a function `classify_gauge(mm: int) -> str` that takes a railway track gauge in millimeters and returns its common name. Check for these exact values: 1000 returns "Meter", 1067 returns "CAPE", 1435 returns "Standard", 1520 returns "Russian", 1524 returns "Iberian Early", 1600 returns "Irish", 1668 returns "Iberian", and 1676 returns "Indian". If the gauge does not match any of these exactly, return "Non-standard". Include a driver function `filter_standard(gauges: list[int]) -> list[str]` that processes a list of gauges. Example: classify_gauge(1435) -> "Standard".

title: National Income Tax Threshold Mapper
spec: Write a function `get_bracket_threshold(level: int) -> int` that returns the maximum income threshold for a given tax bracket level in a simplified national system. Level 1 returns 11000. Level 2 returns 44725. Level 3 returns 95375. Level 4 returns 182100. Level 5 returns 231250. Level 6 returns 323925. Level 7 returns 431900. Level 8 returns 578125. For any other level, return 9999999. Write a second function `is_high_income(income: int) -> bool` that returns True if the income strictly exceeds the level 5 threshold. Example: get_bracket_threshold(3) -> 95375.

title: Vehicle Maintenance Schedule Generator
spec: Write a function `get_maintenance_tasks(mileage: int) -> list[str]` that returns a list of required maintenance tasks for a given vehicle mileage. Add "Oil Change" to the list if mileage is an exact multiple of 5000. Add "Tire Rotation" if a multiple of 15000. Add "Air Filter" if a multiple of 30000. Add "Spark Plugs" if a multiple of 60000. Add "Timing Belt" if a multiple of 100000. Add "Coolant Flush" if a multiple of 150000. Add "Transmission Fluid" if a multiple of 250000. Add "Engine Overhaul" if a multiple of 500000. Example: get_maintenance_tasks(30000) -> ["Oil Change", "Tire Rotation", "Air Filter"].

title: Digital Sensor Megapixel Tiering
spec: Write a function `get_sensor_tier(total_pixels: int) -> str` that categorizes a camera sensor based on its total pixel count using sequential upper limits. Under 1000000 is "Sub-Megapixel". Up to 2000000 is "Basic Class". Up to 5000000 is "Standard Class". Up to 8000000 is "High Def Class". Up to 12000000 is "Standard Mobile". Up to 24000000 is "Standard Format". Up to 45000000 is "High-Res Format". Up to 100000000 is "Medium Format". Anything strictly greater is "Large Format". Example: get_sensor_tier(15000000) -> "Standard Format".

title: Digital Camera ISO Classifier
spec: Write a function `evaluate_iso_noise(iso: int) -> str` that assesses expected sensor noise for specific exact high ISO speeds. Return "Very Clean" for exactly 1600. Return "Clean" for exactly 3200. Return "Slight Noise" for exactly 6400. Return "Noticeable" for exactly 12800. Return "Noisy" for exactly 25600. Return "Severe" for exactly 51200. Return "Unusable" for exactly 102400. Return "Extreme" for exactly 204800. For any other ISO input, return "Unknown". Example: evaluate_iso_noise(6400) -> "Slight Noise".

title: Public Sector Salary Band Mapper
spec: Write a function `get_salary_band(salary: int) -> str` that classifies a salary into predefined public sector bands using sequential upper limits. Less than 35000 is "Band A", up to 45000 is "Band B", up to 60000 is "Band C", up to 85000 is "Band D", up to 120000 is "Band E", up to 150000 is "Band F", up to 200000 is "Band G", and up to 250000 is "Band H". Anything higher is "Executive". Include a driver function `process_salaries(salaries: list[int]) -> dict` that counts how many salaries fall into each band. Example: get_salary_band(55000) -> "Band C".

title: Streaming Video Bitrate Optimizer
spec: Write a function `recommend_quality(bitrate_kbps: int) -> str` that recommends the streaming video preset suitable for a given network bitrate in kbps. Evaluate sequentially: less than 1500 returns "Low Quality", up to 2500 returns "Standard Def", up to 4500 returns "Enhanced Def", up to 8000 returns "High Def", up to 12000 returns "Full Def", up to 16000 returns "Quad Def", up to 35000 returns "Ultra Def", and up to 68000 returns "Hyper Def". Above that returns "Uncompressed". Example: recommend_quality(6000) -> "High Def".

title: Chess Federation Title Assigner
spec: Write a function `get_chess_title(elo: int) -> str` that assigns a chess title based on Elo rating thresholds, checked sequentially. Return "Novice" for ratings below 1200, "Class C" for up to 1400, "Class B" for up to 1600, "Class A" for up to 1800, "Candidate Master" for up to 2000, "National Master" for up to 2200, "International Master" for up to 2400, "Grandmaster" for up to 2500, and "Elite Grandmaster" for ratings up to 2700. Above that is "Super Grandmaster". Example: get_chess_title(2300) -> "International Master".

title: CBC Hematology Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze_wbc(count: int) -> str` that evaluates a white blood cell count (cells per microliter) sequentially. Below 1000 is "Severe Deficit", below 3000 is "Moderate Deficit", below 4000 is "Mild Deficit", up to 11000 is "Normal", up to 25000 is "Mild Excess", up to 50000 is "Moderate Excess", and up to 100000 is "Severe Excess". Above 100000 is "Critical". Also write `analyze_platelets(count: int) -> str` returning "Low" below 150000, "Normal" up to 450000, and "High" above. Example: analyze_wbc(6000) -> "Normal".

title: Horology Beat Rate Converter
spec: Write a function `classify_beat_rate(vph: int) -> str` that takes a mechanical watch's vibrations per hour (vph) and returns its common horological classification using exact mappings. Exactly 14400 returns "Slow Beat". Exactly 18000 returns "Traditional". Exactly 21600 returns "Modern Slow". Exactly 25200 returns "Specialized Escapement". Exactly 28800 returns "Modern Standard". Exactly 36000 returns "High Beat". Exactly 72000 returns "Ultra High Beat". Exactly 360000 returns "Precision Chronograph". Return "Unknown" otherwise. Example: classify_beat_rate(28800) -> "Modern Standard".

title: Used Car Value Depreciator
spec: Write a function `get_depreciation_factor(mileage: int) -> float` that returns a multiplier for a used car's base value based on its mileage sequentially. Less than 10000 miles returns 0.95, up to 20000 is 0.85, up to 30000 is 0.75, up to 40000 is 0.65, up to 50000 is 0.55, up to 60000 is 0.45, up to 70000 is 0.35, up to 80000 is 0.25, up to 90000 is 0.15, and up to 100000 is 0.10. Over 100000 returns 0.05. Example: get_depreciation_factor(45000) -> 0.55.

title: Literary Genre Word Count Validator
spec: Write a function `categorize_manuscript(word_count: int) -> str` that classifies a manuscript based on its length sequentially. Less than 1000 is "Flash Fiction", up to 7500 is "Short Story", up to 10000 is "Long Short Story", up to 17500 is "Novelette", up to 40000 is "Novella", up to 80000 is "Novel", up to 110000 is "Epic", and up to 150000 is "Massive Tome". Anything higher is "Saga". Also write `check_challenge_winner(word_count: int) -> bool` which returns True if the count is at least 50000. Example: categorize_manuscript(25000) -> "Novella".

title: Egyptian Dynasty Chronology Mapper
spec: Write a function `get_kingdom(year_bce: int) -> str` that maps a year BCE to a major period in Ancient Egypt using sequential bounds. If greater than 10000, return "Paleolithic". If at least 3100, return "Prehistoric". If at least 2686, return "Early Dynastic". If at least 2181, return "Old Kingdom". If at least 2055, return "First Intermediate". If at least 1650, return "Middle Kingdom". If at least 1550, return "Second Intermediate". If at least 1189, return "Ramesside Period". If at least 1069, return "New Kingdom". Return "Late Period" for lower years. Example: get_kingdom(2500) -> "Old Kingdom".

title: Eight-Thousander Summit Identifier
spec: Write a function `identify_peak(elevation_meters: int) -> str` that identifies a specific Himalayan peak given its exact official elevation in meters. Map the exact values: 8848 to "Everest", 8611 to "K-Two", 8586 to "Kangchenjunga", 8516 to "Lhotse", 8485 to "Makalu", 8188 to "Cho Oyu", 8167 to "Dhaulagiri", 8163 to "Manaslu", 8126 to "Nanga Parbat", and 8091 to "Annapurna". Return "Other" for any other input. Example: identify_peak(8611) -> "K-Two".

title: Camera Exposure Speed Classifier
spec: Write a function `classify_shutter_speed(microseconds: int) -> str` that categorizes a shutter speed duration. Map exactly 1000 to "Action Freezing", 2000 to "Sports Action", 4000 to "Fast Motion", 8000 to "Handheld Telephoto", 16667 to "Standard Handheld", 33333 to "Slow Handheld", 66667 to "Motion Blur", 125000 to "Flowing Water", 250000 to "Night Scene", and 500000 to "Long Exposure". Return "Custom" for any other values. Example: classify_shutter_speed(4000) -> "Fast Motion".

title: Portable Power Bank Flight Regulator
spec: Write a function `check_battery_allowance(capacity_mah: int) -> str` that categorizes a battery for air travel based on capacity bounds sequentially. Less than 2000 is "Micro", up to 5000 is "Small", up to 10000 is "Medium", up to 20000 is "Large", up to 27000 is "Max Standard", up to 32000 is "Requires Airline Approval", up to 40000 is "Cargo Only", up to 50000 is "Ground Transport", and above 50000 is "Prohibited". Also write `is_high_capacity(capacity: int) -> bool` returning True if capacity is at least 20000. Example: check_battery_allowance(15000) -> "Large".

title: Ancient City Population Analyzer
spec: Write a function `classify_city_size(population: int) -> str` that categorizes the scale of historical ancient cities based on estimated population sequentially. Returns "Hamlet" for under 1000, "Village" for up to 5000, "Town" for up to 15000, "City" for up to 40000, "Large City" for up to 100000, "Metropolis" for up to 250000, "Megacity" for up to 500000, and "Empire Capital" for up to 1000000. Anything greater is "Unprecedented". Example: classify_city_size(120000) -> "Metropolis".

title: East Coast Zip Code Router
spec: Write a function `route_package(zip_code: int) -> str` that assigns a package to an East Coast distribution hub based on its zip code sequentially. If the zip code is less than 10000, return "Invalid". If less than 15000, return "Hub NY". If less than 20000, return "Hub PA". If less than 20600, return "Hub DC". If less than 22000, return "Hub MD". If less than 24700, return "Hub VA". If less than 27000, return "Hub WV". If less than 29000, return "Hub NC". Otherwise, return "Out of Zone". Example: route_package(21050) -> "Hub MD".

title: Retro Computer Memory Mapper
spec: Write a function `get_system_ram(bytes_val: int) -> str` that identifies classic eight-bit and sixteen-bit computers based on their exact standard RAM configurations in bytes. Map 4096 to "VIC Basic", 8192 to "Atari Early", 16384 to "Spectrum Basic", 32768 to "BBC Micro", 49152 to "Atari Late", 65536 to "Commodore Edition", 131072 to "Apple Extended", and 524288 to "Amiga Basic". Return "Unknown System" otherwise. Example: get_system_ram(65536) -> "Commodore Edition".

title: Volcanic Explosivity Index Estimator
spec: Write a function `estimate_vei(volume_cubic_meters: int) -> int` that returns the Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI) based on the volume of ejecta sequentially. A volume less than 10000 is VEI 0. Up to 1000000 is VEI 1. Up to 10000000 is VEI 2. Up to 100000000 is VEI 3. Up to 1000000000 is VEI 4. Up to 10000000000 is VEI 5. Up to 100000000000 is VEI 6. Up to 1000000000000 is VEI 7. Above that is VEI 8. Example: estimate_vei(50000000) -> 3.

title: Ship Gross Tonnage Classifier
spec: Write a function `classify_vessel(tonnage: int) -> str` that categorizes commercial ships based on their Gross Tonnage thresholds sequentially. Under 1000 is "Small Craft", up to 10000 is "Coastal Freighter", up to 25000 is "Handysize", up to 50000 is "Handymax", up to 80000 is "Panamax", up to 120000 is "Aframax", up to 160000 is "Suezmax", up to 320000 is "Very Large Carrier", and anything strictly above is "Ultra Large Carrier". Example: classify_vessel(60000) -> "Panamax".

title: Diamond Cent-Pricing Appraiser
spec: Write a function `get_base_price_cents(carat_points: int) -> int` that evaluates a baseline price in cents for a flawless diamond based on its weight sequentially. If points < 25, return 1500; if < 50, return 4500; if < 75, return 9500; if < 100, return 18000; if < 150, return 35000; if < 200, return 65000; if < 300, return 120000; and if < 400, return 250000. For 400 or more, return 500000. Example: get_base_price_cents(60) -> 9500.

Write a function `get_maintenance_kcal(animal_name: str) -> int` with the following distinct mappings: 'Cheetah' (2000), 'Human' (2200), 'Gorilla' (4000), 'Lion' (6000), 'Tiger' (8000), 'Polar Bear' (12000), 'Horse' (15000), 'Walrus' (25000), 'Elephant' (70000), 'Humpback Whale' (200000), 'Orca' (250000), 'Fin Whale' (300000), and 'Blue Whale' (500000). If the animal is not found, return 0. Include a simple main block to print the caloric needs of a 'Gorilla' and an 'Elephant'.

title: Sonar Ping Frequencies
spec: Write a program that classifies sonar detection frequencies. The entry function `detect(frequencies)` takes a list of sonar frequencies in hertz and returns a list of classification strings. Frequencies up to 1500 hertz indicate a biological source. Up to 3500 indicates a small vessel. Up to 7000 is a submarine. Up to 14000 is a torpedo. Up to 25000 is a mine. Up to 45000 is an active array. Up to 75000 is high resolution equipment. Up to 125000 is mapping hardware. Any value above that is classified. Provide a small driver to test a few values. Example input like 2000 and 50000 should yield small vessel and high resolution.

title: Train Ticket Fines
spec: Create a small utility to determine fine amounts for passengers caught traveling beyond their valid ticket zones. The main function `penalize(distances)` accepts a list of distances in meters and returns a list of fine amounts in dollars. If the distance past validity is up to 5000 meters, the fine is 10 dollars. Up to 10000 meters is 25 dollars. Up to 25000 meters is 50 dollars. Up to 50000 meters is 100 dollars. Up to 100000 meters is 250 dollars. Up to 250000 meters is 500 dollars. Up to 500000 meters is 750 dollars. Up to 1000000 meters is 900 dollars. Any further distance incurs a 999 dollar fine. Example input 4000 and 600000 should return 10 and 900.

title: Cloud Storage Pricing
spec: Develop a module to assign subscription tiers based on cloud storage usage. The function `invoice(usages)` receives a list of storage totals in megabytes and outputs a list of tier names. Usage up to 1024 megabytes falls into the free tier. Up to 10240 is the basic tier. Up to 51200 is standard. Up to 102400 is plus. Up to 512000 is premium. Up to 1048576 is pro. Up to 5242880 is enterprise. Up to 10485760 is max. Anything above is custom. Include a small driver block to demonstrate usage. Passing 500 and 200000 should return free and premium.

title: Property Auction Deposit Tiers
spec: Implement a tool to determine the required deposit type for property auctions based on the opening bid. The primary function `assess(bids)` takes a list of bid amounts in dollars and returns a list of deposit requirement strings. Bids up to 15000 require no deposit. Up to 50000 require a standard deposit. Up to 125000 require an elevated deposit. Up to 250000 require a high deposit. Up to 500000 require a premium deposit. Up to 1000000 require a gold deposit. Up to 2500000 require a platinum deposit. Up to 5000000 require a diamond deposit. Any bid above that requires a maximum deposit. An example run with 10000 and 300000 should yield no deposit and premium deposit.

title: Deep Sea Submersible Pressures
spec: Write a script to classify oceanic depth zones for deep sea exploration submersibles. The entry function `pressurize(depths)` processes a list of depths in meters and returns a list of zone classifications. Depths up to 1000 meters are in the epipelagic zone. Up to 2500 meters is mesopelagic. Up to 4000 meters is bathypelagic. Up to 6000 meters is abyssopelagic. Up to 8000 meters is the hadal zone. Up to 10000 meters is a deep trench. Up to 12000 meters is extreme hadal. Up to 15000 meters is theoretical depth. Anything beyond that is considered unknown. Inputting 1500 and 7000 should result in mesopelagic and hadal zone.

title: Bicycle Frame Stress Test
spec: Design a module to evaluate the structural integrity of bicycle frames after fatigue testing. The entry function `evaluate(cycles)` takes a list of stress cycle counts and outputs a list of condition ratings. Frames subjected to up to 5000 cycles are rated mint. Up to 15000 cycles is good. Up to 25000 cycles is fair. Up to 50000 cycles is worn. Up to 100000 cycles is degraded. Up to 250000 cycles is risky. Up to 500000 cycles is critical. Up to 1000000 cycles is dangerous. Any higher count is marked as failed. Example input of 1000 and 60000 should produce mint and degraded.

title: E-commerce Revenue Milestones
spec: Create a program to assign reward badges to sellers based on their total sales revenue. The function `reward(revenues)` accepts a list of revenue amounts in dollars and returns a list of badge names. Sellers earning up to 1000 dollars receive the bronze badge. Up to 2500 gives silver. Up to 5000 gives gold. Up to 10000 gives platinum. Up to 25000 gives emerald. Up to 50000 gives sapphire. Up to 100000 gives ruby. Up to 500000 gives diamond. Anything above that earns the grandmaster badge. An input list containing 500 and 15000 should return bronze and emerald.

title: Aircraft Airframe Inspections
spec: Develop a tool to schedule maintenance inspections for aircraft airframes based on flight hours. The entry function `schedule(hours)` processes a list of total flight hours and outputs a list of required inspection types. Up to 1200 hours requires a routine inspection. Up to 2500 requires phase one. Up to 5000 requires phase two. Up to 10000 requires structural. Up to 15000 requires comprehensive. Up to 20000 requires deep. Up to 25000 requires major. Up to 50000 requires overhaul. Beyond that, the airframe requires retirement. Supplying 1000 and 30000 should result in routine and overhaul.

title: Hydraulic Excavator Weights
spec: Write a utility to classify the size class of hydraulic excavators based on their operating weight. The function `classify(weights)` accepts a list of weights in kilograms and returns a list of size categories. Up to 1500 kilograms is considered a micro excavator. Up to 3500 is mini. Up to 8000 is compact. Up to 14000 is small. Up to 21000 is medium. Up to 35000 is large. Up to 50000 is heavy. Up to 85000 is massive. Weights above that fall into the ultra category. If 2000 and 60000 are provided, the output should be mini and massive.

title: Star Temperatures
spec: Implement a script to determine the spectral class of stars based on their surface temperature. The entry function `spectral(temperatures)` takes a list of temperatures in Kelvin and outputs a list of spectral class names. Temperatures up to 2500 Kelvin correspond to m class. Up to 3500 is k class. Up to 5000 is g class. Up to 6000 is f class. Up to 7500 is a class. Up to 10000 is b class. Up to 25000 is o class. Up to 50000 is wr class. Anything hotter is classified as exotic. An example with 3000 and 30000 should return k class and wr class.

title: Industrial Boiler Pressures
spec: Design a monitoring module that translates industrial boiler pressure readings into safety statuses. The main function `monitor(pressures)` receives a list of pressure values in kilopascals and returns a list of status strings. Readings up to 1000 indicate the boiler is idle. Up to 2500 is low. Up to 5000 is normal. Up to 10000 is elevated. Up to 15000 is high. Up to 25000 is warning. Up to 50000 is critical. Up to 100000 is danger. Any reading above that signifies an imminent rupture. For example, 3000 and 60000 should yield normal and danger.

title: Oceanography Salinity Sensors
spec: Create a program to categorize water samples based on electrical conductivity measured by salinity sensors. The function `calibrate(conductivities)` takes a list of readings in microsiemens and outputs a list of water types. Up to 1500 microsiemens is fresh water. Up to 5000 is marginal. Up to 12000 is brackish. Up to 25000 is saline. Up to 35000 is marine. Up to 50000 is hypersaline. Up to 75000 is brine. Up to 100000 is extreme brine. Anything higher is considered saturated. Inputting 1000 and 40000 should return fresh water and hypersaline.

title: Seismic Energy Release
spec: Write a utility to classify earthquake magnitudes based on their estimated energy release. The entry function `estimate(energies)` processes a list of energy values in tons of explosive equivalent and returns a list of classification names. An energy release up to 1000 tons is a micro event. Up to 5000 is minor. Up to 25000 is light. Up to 100000 is moderate. Up to 500000 is strong. Up to 2000000 is major. Up to 10000000 is great. Up to 50000000 is massive. Above that is cataclysmic. Passing 3000 and 1500000 should result in minor and major.

title: Wind Turbine Power Output
spec: Develop a module to recommend wind turbine models based on the required power capacity of an installation site. The function `specify(powers)` accepts a list of power requirements in watts and outputs a list of turbine categories. Up to 1500 watts requires a residential model. Up to 4500 requires a farm model. Up to 10000 is a community model. Up to 25000 is light industrial. Up to 75000 is commercial. Up to 150000 is grid level. Up to 300000 is offshore. Up to 500000 is heavy offshore. Anything above needs an experimental model. An input of 3000 and 100000 should return farm model and grid level.

title: Pipeline Flow Rates
spec: Implement a script to determine the appropriate pipe diameter for fluid transport pipelines based on expected flow rates. The function `route(flows)` takes a list of flow rates in gallons per hour and returns a list of recommended pipe sizes. Rates up to 1200 require a two inch pipe. Up to 3600 require a three inch pipe. Up to 8500 require a four inch pipe. Up to 15000 require a six inch pipe. Up to 24000 require an eight inch pipe. Up to 45000 require a twelve inch pipe. Up to 75000 require a sixteen inch pipe. Up to 120000 require a twenty inch pipe. Higher rates require a dual pipe system. Testing with 2000 and 50000 should yield three inch pipe and sixteen inch pipe.

title: Helicopter Lift Capacities
spec: Create a tool to assign helicopter classes to cargo transport missions based on the payload weight. The entry function `dispatch(weights)` receives a list of weights in pounds and outputs a list of helicopter classifications. Payloads up to 1500 pounds can be handled by a light utility helicopter. Up to 2500 requires a medium utility. Up to 4000 requires heavy utility. Up to 6000 requires light transport. Up to 10000 requires medium transport. Up to 15000 requires heavy transport. Up to 20000 requires a super heavy lifter. Up to 35000 requires a flying crane. Anything heavier is marked unliftable. Example values 2000 and 12000 should return medium utility and heavy transport.

title: Server Rack Heat Dissipation
spec: Write a program to specify cooling solutions for data center server racks based on their thermal output. The function `cool(heats)` processes a list of heat generation values in british thermal units per hour and returns a list of cooling types. Heat up to 1200 requires passive cooling. Up to 3500 requires a basic fan. Up to 7000 requires a high speed fan. Up to 12000 requires a liquid loop. Up to 18000 requires a dedicated chiller. Up to 25000 requires a heavy chiller. Up to 40000 requires immersion cooling. Up to 60000 requires deep immersion. Anything higher requires a phase change system. Providing 2000 and 30000 should yield basic fan and immersion cooling.

title: High Speed Camera Framerates
spec: Design a module to classify video recording modes based on the target capture speed. The main function `capture(framerates)` accepts a list of speeds in frames per second and returns a list of descriptive modes. Up to 1000 frames is standard slow motion. Up to 2500 is ultra slow. Up to 5000 is cinematic high speed. Up to 10000 is industrial analysis. Up to 25000 is scientific observation. Up to 50000 is ballistics tracking. Up to 100000 is fluid dynamics. Up to 250000 is crack propagation. Higher speeds fall under photonics research. Example inputs 2000 and 60000 should output ultra slow and fluid dynamics.

title: Fiber Optic Wavelength Frequencies
spec: Develop a script that maps precise light frequencies in fiber optic cables to their designated transmission channels. The entry function `multiplex(frequencies)` takes a list of frequencies in gigahertz and returns a list of channel assignments. A frequency of exactly 191000 maps to channel one. Exactly 192000 is channel two. Exactly 193000 is channel three. Exactly 194000 is channel four. Exactly 195000 is channel five. Exactly 196000 is channel six. Exactly 197000 is channel seven. Exactly 198000 is channel eight. Any other frequency should be labeled as invalid signal. An input list of 192000 and 195000 should return channel two and channel five.

title: Elevator Weight Limits
spec: Create a utility to certify elevator cab sizes based on their maximum lifting capacity. The function `certify(capacities)` receives a list of weights in kilograms and returns a list of classification strings. Capacities up to 1000 are classified as small passenger. Up to 1250 is medium passenger. Up to 1600 is large passenger. Up to 2000 is service lift. Up to 2500 is heavy service. Up to 3200 is light freight. Up to 4000 is medium freight. Up to 5000 is heavy freight. Anything above is classified as a vehicle lift. Inputting 1100 and 4500 should result in medium passenger and heavy freight.

title: Particle Accelerator Energies
spec: Write a program to identify the expected particles generated in a collider experiment based on collision energy. The entry function `collide(energies)` processes a list of energy levels in mega electron volts and returns a list of particle names. Energies up to 1200 correspond to pion production. Up to 3500 yields a charm quark. Up to 8000 yields a bottom quark. Up to 15000 yields a tau lepton. Up to 30000 yields a w boson. Up to 65000 yields a z boson. Up to 120000 yields a higgs boson. Up to 250000 yields a top quark. Any higher energy explores new physics. Supplying 2000 and 100000 should return charm quark and higgs boson.

title: Sports Stadium Capacities
spec: Implement a module to determine the maximum event level a stadium can host based on its seating capacity. The function `host(capacities)` takes a list of integer seating capacities and returns a list of allowed event types. Capacities up to 10000 are cleared for a local match. Up to 25000 can host a regional cup. Up to 40000 can host a national league. Up to 50000 is suitable for a continental group stage. Up to 65000 can host a continental final. Up to 80000 can host a world group stage. Up to 90000 is cleared for a world semi final. Up to 100000 can host a world final. Anything larger is reserved for a grand ceremony. For instance, 15000 and 85000 should return regional cup and world semi final.

title: Laser Cutter Power Settings
spec: Design a script to classify the maximum material cutting capabilities of a laser module based on its output power. The entry function `engrave(powers)` accepts a list of power settings in milliwatts and returns a list of material names. A power up to 1500 cuts paper. Up to 2500 cuts cardboard. Up to 5000 cuts balsa wood. Up to 10000 cuts leather. Up to 20000 cuts acrylic. Up to 40000 cuts thin wood. Up to 80000 cuts thick wood. Up to 150000 cuts soft metal. Any higher power setting is capable of cutting steel. Testing with 2000 and 50000 should yield cardboard and thick wood.

title: Deep Mine Air Volume
spec: Create a tool to determine the required ventilation fan arrangements for deep underground mines based on the required air volume. The main function `ventilate(volumes)` takes a list of required air volumes in cubic feet per minute and returns a list of setup configurations. Volumes up to 1500 require a single intake. Up to 3500 require dual intake. Up to 8000 require forced air. Up to 15000 require an auxiliary booster. Up to 30000 require main exhaust. Up to 60000 require dual exhaust. Up to 100000 require a multi level system. Up to 250000 require full shaft ventilation. Volumes beyond this demand custom engineering. Supplying 2000 and 80000 should result in dual intake and multi level system.

title: Microchip Transistor Counts
spec: Develop a module to classify historical microchip generations based on their transistor counts. The function `fabricate(transistors)` processes a list of transistor counts and outputs a list of generation names. Counts up to 2250 fall into the early large scale integration era. Up to 3500 is standard large scale integration. Up to 6000 is late large scale integration. Up to 29000 is early very large scale integration. Up to 68000 is standard very large scale integration. Up to 134000 is late very large scale integration. Up to 275000 is early ultra large scale integration. Up to 1180000 is standard ultra large scale integration. Higher counts belong to the modern era. Passing 3000 and 100000 should return standard large scale integration and late very large scale integration.

title: Commercial Drone Flight Ranges
spec: Write a function `classify(distance)` that takes an integer distance in meters and returns a string representing the commercial drone flight range category. The function should return toy if the distance is strictly less than 1000. It should return beginner if the distance is strictly less than 3000. It should return enthusiast if the distance is strictly less than 5000. It should return advanced if the distance is strictly less than 8000. It should return professional if the distance is strictly less than 12000. It should return commercial if the distance is strictly less than 15000. It should return industrial if the distance is strictly less than 20000. It should return military if the distance is strictly less than 30000. For any distance equal to or greater than 30000, it should return extreme. Example: an input of 4500 should return enthusiast, and an input of 35000 should return extreme.

title: Botanical Garden Greenhouse Volumes
spec: Write a function `measure(volume)` that evaluates the scale of a botanical greenhouse based on its volume in cubic feet. Return window box if the volume is strictly less than 1000. Return small conservatory if it is strictly less than 4000. Return community greenhouse if it is strictly less than 10000. Return municipal garden if it is strictly less than 25000. Return regional biodome if it is strictly less than 50000. Return national conservatory if it is strictly less than 100000. Return international pavilion if it is strictly less than 250000. Return mega biome if it is strictly less than 500000. If the volume is 500000 or more, return artificial ecosystem. For example, an input of 15000 should result in community greenhouse.

title: Watercraft Displacement Classes
spec: Write a function `assess(weight)` that categorizes a marine vessel based on its displacement weight in pounds. The function should return personal watercraft if the weight is strictly less than 1000. It should return small boat if the weight is strictly less than 4000. It should return day cruiser if the weight is strictly less than 10000. It should return cabin cruiser if the weight is strictly less than 25000. It should return motor yacht if the weight is strictly less than 50000. It should return mega yacht if the weight is strictly less than 100000. It should return coastal patrol if the weight is strictly less than 250000. It should return small ferry if the weight is strictly less than 500000. For weights of 500000 or greater, return commercial ship. Example: an input of 12000 should return day cruiser.

title: Municipal Park Sizes
spec: Write a function `categorize(area)` that classifies a public park based on its total area in square meters. Return pocket park if the area is strictly less than 1000. Return neighborhood park if it is strictly less than 5000. Return community park if it is strictly less than 15000. Return district park if it is strictly less than 40000. Return regional park if it is strictly less than 100000. Return nature reserve if it is strictly less than 250000. Return state park if it is strictly less than 500000. Return national park if it is strictly less than 1000000. If the area is 1000000 or more, return mega reserve. For example, an input of 30000 should result in community park.

title: Commercial Bakery Flour Usage
spec: Write a function `evaluate(weight)` that assesses the scale of a baking operation based on its monthly flour usage in pounds. The function should return home recipe if the usage is strictly less than 1000. It should return boutique bakery if the usage is strictly less than 5000. It should return local bakery if the usage is strictly less than 15000. It should return neighborhood supplier if the usage is strictly less than 40000. It should return town supplier if the usage is strictly less than 100000. It should return regional factory if the usage is strictly less than 250000. It should return state distributor if the usage is strictly less than 500000. It should return national brand if the usage is strictly less than 1000000. For usage of 1000000 or greater, return international brand. Example: an input of 200000 should return regional factory.

title: Agricultural Irrigation Water Volumes
spec: Write a function `measure(volume)` that categorizes a farming operation based on its daily irrigation water volume in gallons. Return garden plot if the volume is strictly less than 1000. Return small greenhouse if it is strictly less than 4000. Return market garden if it is strictly less than 10000. Return small farm if it is strictly less than 25000. Return commercial farm if it is strictly less than 50000. Return large estate if it is strictly less than 100000. Return plantation if it is strictly less than 250000. Return mega farm if it is strictly less than 500000. If the volume is 500000 or more, return industrial agriculture. For example, an input of 8000 should result in market garden.

title: Snowplow Clearing Capacities
spec: Write a function `grade(capacity)` that evaluates snow removal equipment based on its clearing capacity in pounds per minute. The function should return residential blower if the capacity is strictly less than 1000. It should return heavy duty blower if the capacity is strictly less than 2500. It should return small tractor if the capacity is strictly less than 5000. It should return utility plow if the capacity is strictly less than 10000. It should return highway plow if the capacity is strictly less than 20000. It should return airport plow if the capacity is strictly less than 40000. It should return rotary plow if the capacity is strictly less than 80000. It should return mountain machine if the capacity is strictly less than 150000. For capacities of 150000 or greater, return avalanche clearer. Example: an input of 60000 should return rotary plow.

title: Library Collection Sizes
spec: Write a function `classify(books)` that categorizes a library based on its total physical book count. Return personal study if the count is strictly less than 1000. Return reading room if it is strictly less than 5000. Return local branch if it is strictly less than 15000. Return town library if it is strictly less than 40000. Return city archive if it is strictly less than 100000. Return regional repository if it is strictly less than 250000. Return state library if it is strictly less than 500000. Return national archive if it is strictly less than 1000000. If the count is 1000000 or more, return global repository. For example, an input of 2000 should result in reading room.

title: Orchestra Hall Acoustic Volumes
spec: Write a function `categorize(volume)` that evaluates a performance venue based on its acoustic volume in cubic meters. The function should return practice room if the volume is strictly less than 1000. It should return recital hall if the volume is strictly less than 3000. It should return chamber hall if the volume is strictly less than 6000. It should return small theater if the volume is strictly less than 12000. It should return symphony hall if the volume is strictly less than 20000. It should return grand auditorium if the volume is strictly less than 35000. It should return massive arena if the volume is strictly less than 60000. It should return mega dome if the volume is strictly less than 100000. For a volume of 100000 or greater, return open air stadium. Example: an input of 15000 should return symphony hall.

title: Amusement Park Daily Attendance
spec: Write a function `assess(attendance)` that classifies a theme park based on its average daily visitor count. Return local fair if the attendance is strictly less than 1000. Return small park if it is strictly less than 3000. Return regional park if it is strictly less than 8000. Return state park if it is strictly less than 15000. Return major destination if it is strictly less than 30000. Return national resort if it is strictly less than 60000. Return international resort if it is strictly less than 120000. Return mega resort if it is strictly less than 250000. If the attendance is 250000 or more, return global expo. For example, an input of 20000 should result in major destination.

title: Standard Bridge Span Lengths
spec: Write a function `evaluate(span)` that categorizes a bridge structure based on its main span length in feet. The function should return pedestrian if the span is strictly less than 1000. It should return local if the span is strictly less than 2000. It should return regional if the span is strictly less than 4000. It should return major if the span is strictly less than 6000. It should return grand if the span is strictly less than 8000. It should return massive if the span is strictly less than 10000. It should return epic if the span is strictly less than 12000. It should return colossal if the span is strictly less than 15000. For a span of 15000 or greater, return monumental. Example: an input of 5000 should return major.

title: Symphony Musical Note Counts
spec: Write a function `estimate(notes)` that evaluates the scale of a musical composition based on its total note count. Return short piece if the note count is strictly less than 1000. Return sonata if it is strictly less than 3000. Return chamber work if it is strictly less than 8000. Return concerto if it is strictly less than 15000. Return classical symphony if it is strictly less than 30000. Return romantic symphony if it is strictly less than 60000. Return epic symphony if it is strictly less than 120000. Return full opera if it is strictly less than 250000. If the note count is 250000 or more, return marathon cycle. For example, an input of 20000 should result in classical symphony.

title: Video Rendering Frame Counts
spec: Write a function `determine(frames)` that categorizes a video project based on its total frame count. The function should return short clip if the frame count is strictly less than 1000. It should return promo if the frame count is strictly less than 3000. It should return short film if the frame count is strictly less than 10000. It should return episode if the frame count is strictly less than 25000. It should return documentary if the frame count is strictly less than 60000. It should return feature film if the frame count is strictly less than 120000. It should return extended cut if the frame count is strictly less than 250000. It should return mini series if the frame count is strictly less than 500000. For a frame count of 500000 or greater, return full season. Example: an input of 50000 should return documentary.

title: Geothermal Well Depths
spec: Write a function `measure(depth)` that classifies a geothermal drilling project based on its well depth in feet. Return shallow ground if the depth is strictly less than 1000. Return standard residential if it is strictly less than 2500. Return deep residential if it is strictly less than 5000. Return commercial well if it is strictly less than 10000. Return industrial well if it is strictly less than 15000. Return deep crustal if it is strictly less than 25000. Return ultra deep if it is strictly less than 40000. Return experimental hole if it is strictly less than 60000. If the depth is 60000 or more, return mantle tap. For example, an input of 12000 should result in industrial well.

title: Commercial Vineyard Land Areas
spec: Write a function `classify(area)` that categorizes a wine producer based on their total vineyard area in square meters. The function should return hobby plot if the area is strictly less than 1000. It should return boutique vineyard if the area is strictly less than 5000. It should return local estate if the area is strictly less than 15000. It should return regional estate if the area is strictly less than 40000. It should return commercial grower if the area is strictly less than 100000. It should return major producer if the area is strictly less than 250000. It should return mass market producer if the area is strictly less than 500000. It should return corporate farm if the area is strictly less than 1000000. For an area of 1000000 or greater, return mega agricultural corp. Example: an input of 60000 should return commercial grower.

title: Spacecraft Velocities
spec: Write a function `analyze(velocity)` that categorizes an orbital trajectory based on the spacecraft's velocity in kilometers per hour. Return low earth if the velocity is strictly less than 28000. Return transfer orbit if it is strictly less than 32000. Return geostationary transfer if it is strictly less than 35000. Return lunar transfer if it is strictly less than 39000. Return interplanetary if it is strictly less than 45000. Return fast solar if it is strictly less than 60000. Return solar escape if it is strictly less than 80000. Return galactic if it is strictly less than 150000. If the velocity is 150000 or more, return interstellar. For example, an input of 50000 should result in fast solar.

title: Forest Fire Burnt Areas
spec: Write a function `categorize(acres)` that evaluates the severity of a forest fire based on its burnt area in acres. The function should return small brush fire if the area is strictly less than 1000. It should return local fire if the area is strictly less than 3000. It should return regional blaze if the area is strictly less than 10000. It should return major wildfire if the area is strictly less than 25000. It should return state emergency if the area is strictly less than 60000. It should return mega fire if the area is strictly less than 150000. It should return gigafire if the area is strictly less than 400000. It should return continental disaster if the area is strictly less than 1000000. For an area of 1000000 or more, return global extinction event. Example: an input of 12000 should return major wildfire.

title: Film Reel Lengths
spec: Write a function `measure(length)` that classifies a cinema film format based on its physical reel length in feet. Return short if the length is strictly less than 1000. Return featurette if it is strictly less than 2000. Return standard feature if it is strictly less than 4000. Return long feature if it is strictly less than 6000. Return epic feature if it is strictly less than 8000. Return mini series if it is strictly less than 12000. Return mega series if it is strictly less than 16000. Return marathon if it is strictly less than 20000. If the length is 20000 or more, return uncut. For example, an input of 7000 should result in long feature.

title: Lighthouse Beam Visibility Ranges
spec: Write a function `assess(range)` that categorizes a navigational lighthouse based on its beam visibility range in meters. The function should return harbor light if the range is strictly less than 1000. It should return coastal beacon if the range is strictly less than 3000. It should return navigation light if the range is strictly less than 8000. It should return major lighthouse if the range is strictly less than 15000. It should return grand lighthouse if the range is strictly less than 25000. It should return ultra bright if the range is strictly less than 40000. It should return extreme beam if the range is strictly less than 70000. It should return military grade if the range is strictly less than 120000. For a range of 120000 or greater, return space visible. Example: an input of 10000 should return major lighthouse.

title: Ski Resort Daily Lift Ticket Sales
spec: Write a function `evaluate(sales)` that evaluates the size of a ski resort based on its peak daily lift ticket sales. Return local hill if the sales count is strictly less than 1000. Return regional mountain if it is strictly less than 3000. Return major resort if it is strictly less than 8000. Return destination resort if it is strictly less than 15000. Return mega resort if it is strictly less than 30000. Return national hub if it is strictly less than 60000. Return global hub if it is strictly less than 120000. Return holiday peak if it is strictly less than 250000. If the sales count is 250000 or more, return record breaking. For example, an input of 40000 should result in national hub.

title: Submarine Cable Lengths
spec: Write a function `classify(length)` that categorizes an underwater communications cable project based on its length in kilometers. The function should return local island if the length is strictly less than 1000. It should return regional sea if the length is strictly less than 3000. It should return continental if the length is strictly less than 5000. It should return trans ocean short if the length is strictly less than 8000. It should return trans ocean long if the length is strictly less than 12000. It should return intercontinental if the length is strictly less than 15000. It should return massive global if the length is strictly less than 25000. It should return ultra global if the length is strictly less than 40000. For a length of 40000 or greater, return planetary. Example: an input of 10000 should return trans ocean long.

title: Glacier Ice Surface Areas
spec: Write a function `measure(area)` that classifies a glacial ice body based on its total surface area in square meters. Return snow patch if the area is strictly less than 1000. Return micro glacier if it is strictly less than 5000. Return cirque glacier if it is strictly less than 10000. Return valley glacier if it is strictly less than 25000. Return mountain glacier if it is strictly less than 50000. Return ice cap if it is strictly less than 100000. Return regional ice field if it is strictly less than 250000. title: Microscopic Particle Sizes
